findings.text: follow-on: the assertions `assert "value" not in data` and `assert "values" not in data` (lines 61-62) are plan s3's done-when clause that no signal value property was touched, but they cannot fail against that regression: FacilitySignal (imas_codex/schemas/facility.yaml, class FacilitySignal) declares neither a value nor a values attribute, and data is built with model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True) which drops unset optionals, so a newly declared value property would be dropped before the assertion and the test would stay green.

follow-on: the new COCOSClass enum re-declares the seven non-trivial COCOS labels (psi_like, dodpsi_like, ip_like, b0_like, q_like, tor_angle_like, pol_angle_like) that imas_codex/schemas/imas_dd.yaml:100 COCOSLabelTransformation already owns, as an independent parallel list, so the two can drift if either label's spelling or meaning changes; plan s3 fixes this facility-side enum as the design, so it is recorded rather than repaired here.

follow_ons: Two node-local follow-ons, both non-blocking and neither requiring repair in this review's write scope: (1) strengthen tests/graph/test_signal_convention_schema.py:61-62 so the 'no signal value property touched' claim is asserted by a mechanism that could fail (assert on the SignalSource/FacilitySignal field set directly instead of on a dump that drops unset optional fields); (2) note the deliberate duplication between COCOSClass (imas_codex/schemas/facility.yaml:242) and COCOSLabelTransformation (imas_codex/schemas/imas_dd.yaml:100) so label spelling stays in step. Separately, the four live-graph compliance failures are pre-existing and outside this node's declared scope (StandardName deletion labels/properties, WikiPage.embed_failed_at, DDResolution/FacilityPath/Unit nulls), reported by the node under its own follow_ons, and belong to the schema/data owners it named.
